articles.headline: From Cape Island (letter)
articles.author: Sea Side (pseud.)
articles.summary: At this place the season is backward, both as to people and weather. Reports on the Cape Island (Cape May, N.J.) summer resort season; notes the 'Banneker' House. Rev. Stephen Smith has induced resident Christians to repair the temple of worship. Miss Fanny Jackson, Principal of the Female Department of the Institute for Colored Youth, is stopping at the residence of Rev. Stephen Smith; she lectured Tuesday evening, July 23d, introduced by Sam'l Whipper, Esq. Dated July 24, 1867.
people: Principal, Female Dept., Institute for Colored Youth (Miss); lectured at Cape Island

articles.headline: Letter (reply to Rev. T. Gould on camp-meetings / the A.M.E. Union Camp)
articles.author: D. P. Seaton
articles.summary: Replies to Rev. T. Gould's communication of August 3d about camp-meetings, especially the A.M.E. Union Camp; notes Gould was present at the preacher's meeting in Philadelphia where the matter was discussed. Defends the Union Camp as held for the glory of God. Signed D. P. Seaton, Frankford, Phila.

articles.headline: Let every preacher in the A.M.E. Church read this again and again (Book Concern $7000 appeal)
articles.summary: Editorial appeal to raise $7000 by mid-September or Oct 1 to pay off the Book Concern debt. Names District Book Stewards: Dr. W. T. Revels (Missouri), W. C. Trevan (Indiana), John Turner (Louisiana), Samuel Watts (Ohio), William D. W. Schureman (Baltimore), Denton Dorrell (Philadelphia Conference), Henry Davis (New York), John W. Earley (New England), R. H. Cain (S. Carolina), H. M. Turner (Georgia), Thomas M. D. Ward (California), G. T. Watkins (Virginia). The Book Committee met July 1st and apportioned the $7000 (total $7025): Philadelphia District $1000. Elisha Weaver pledges $100.

articles.headline: Report of Committee on Aid for the Book Concern ($7,000 must be raised)
articles.summary: Committee report, by order of the Conference, proposing a plan to liquidate the Book Concern's debt: each pastor to assess his charge, funds sent by express to Rev. Elisha Weaver, Box 2975, Philadelphia. Signed E. Weaver, Chairman; Stephen Smith, Treasurer; H. J. Rhodes, Secretary; J. M. Williams, J. Mitchell, Wm. Moore.

articles.headline: Notice -- agent appointed for the new Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church
articles.summary: To all whom it may concern: This is to certify that Mr. W. F. Dickerson, one of the students of Lincoln College, Oxford, Pa., is appointed an agent to collect money for the new Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church. Signed in behalf of the Trustees and members, H. J. R[hodes], Minister-in-Charge.
people: appointed collecting agent; student, Lincoln College, Oxford Pa
Minister-in-Charge, Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church (Rev.); surname partly obscured, matches p2 H. J. Rhodes

articles.headline: Notice -- revocation of James Bowers's license (Macedonia A.M.E., Camden)
articles.author: J. B. Hamilton
articles.summary: This is to certify that James Bowers, formerly a preacher of Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J., is a refractory preacher and has left his church under censure; therefore his licenses in behalf of the named church are null and void. J. B. Hamilton, Elder-in-Charge. July 25th, 1867.
people: former preacher, Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden N.J.; license revoked

articles.headline: Deaths (Philadelphia)
articles.summary: Brother Benjamin Bell, one of the oldest members and class-leaders of Bethel church, expired very suddenly last Sabbath; he went to church twice that day, sat down on his door-step on reaching home and died in a few moments. Also: at Frankford, Pa., July 7th, 1867, Elizabeth S. ('Lizzie'), infant daughter of George and Elizabeth Pleasant, aged 9 months, 2 weeks and 1 day.
people: deceased; oldest member and class-leader, Bethel church

articles.headline: Advertisement -- Freedman's Cheap Store, Beaufort, S.C. (Smalls & Gleaves)
articles.summary: FREEDMAN'S CHEAP STORE, [P.?] between 4th and 5th Streets, Beaufort, S.C. Wholesale and retail dealers in provisions and groceries, dry goods, trimmings, boots, shoes and notions; highest market prices paid for Sea Island Cotton. Proprietors printed 'Capt. R. Smalls' and 'R. [H./D.] Gleaves'; firm name 'Smalls & Gleaves, Beaufort, S.C.' NON-Philadelphia, but captured for the Robert Smalls watch and the R. H. Gleaves (former Philadelphian) connection. (Repeats in the 08-17, 08-24, 08-31 issues; the Gleaves initial reads more like 'R. H.' in the 08-17 printing.)
people: proprietor, Freedman's Cheap Store, Beaufort S.C. (Capt.); almost certainly Robert Smalls
proprietor, Freedman's Cheap Store, Beaufort S.C.; printed 'R. D./R. H.', very likely R. H. Gleaves of Philadelphia

articles.headline: Advertisement -- dental office of the late Dr. Jos. Mc. C. Crummill offered (Sarah Mc. C. Crummill)
articles.summary: A Rare Chance for a First-Class Dentist. Wanted, a first-class surgical and mechanical dentist to take the office and laboratory of the late Dr. Jos. Mc. C. Crummill, who for over twenty years occupied the premises and carried on the business. For terms apply to Sarah Mc. C. Crummill, 449 North Third Street, Philadelphia. (Standing ad; also appears Aug 17.)
people: advertiser; widow offering the dental office, 449 North Third Street

articles.headline: Acknowledgements (for Rev. Theodore Gould, Travelling Agent)
articles.summary: Receipts acknowledged for the Recorder and for Rev. Theodore Gould, Travelling Agent, from New York (Rev. H. Davis), Parkesburg Pa (B. Thomas), Charleston S.C. (J. Wilson), Pittsburgh (Rev. Jas. A. Shorter), Cleveland (M. A. Lynch), and from New Jersey points (Salem, Yorktown, Woodstown) and Oxford Pa. Subscriber/donor names mostly common and out-of-town (listed in text, not linked).
people: travelling agent, Christian Recorder / Book Concern (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice -- system for cutting and fitting ladies' and children's clothing (756 S. Eighth St.)
articles.summary: An elegant and easy system for cutting and fitting ladies' and children's clothing can be learned in half an hour, at 756 South Eighth Street, below Fitzwater. Agents wanted. Dated aug3-1m (no proprietor named). Repeats Aug 17.

articles.headline: How We Spent Last Sabbath (editor's visit to the Home for Aged and to Camden)
articles.summary: At half past ten o'clock we preached at the Old Folks' Home; sorry to find Mother Boggs and a number of the others much indisposed. In the afternoon we went over to Camden, New Jersey, to assist Brother Hamilton in the administration of the Lord's Supper; the congregation much increased, and expected to come up strongly for the $7025.
people: resident, Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons (reported indisposed)

articles.headline: Notice -- Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons (appeal for contributions)
articles.summary: The Board of Managers of the Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons is in great need of funds. Contributions may be left with the matron at the Home, or with Samuel R. Skipp, No. 111 South Fourth St.; Rev. William Alston, rector of St. Thomas' church; Henry Gordon, Rodman St.; or Rev. Stephen Smith, Lombard St.
people: receiver of contributions, No. 111 South Fourth St.
rector of St. Thomas' church (Rev.); receiver of contributions

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Sandy Wilson)
articles.author: Sandy Wilson
articles.summary: Information wanted of my mother, Margaret Jones; she belonged to Benjamin Lockhardt, of Berkeley county, Va. Also my brother Benjamin Lockhardt (his wife's name was Peggy); Charles Rose, John A. Rose, Israel Rose; my sister Lucy Wells, married to James Wells; Harriet Lisle, wife of William Lisle; also Hester Rose and Eliza Rose. Address Sandy Wilson, No. 6 Poplar Court, running from Currant Alley above Locust street, between 10th and 11th streets. (Phila inquirer; sought persons formerly enslaved in Berkeley co., Va.)
people: inquirer; No. 6 Poplar Court (off Currant Alley, above Locust, between 10th and 11th), Philadelphia
sought (mother); formerly enslaved, Berkeley co. Va
sought (brother); formerly enslaved, Berkeley co. Va

articles.headline: Wanted -- place to learn a trade (W. A. Rice)
articles.summary: Wanted, by a well-raised colored boy, a place to learn a trade in Philadelphia, Washington, Baltimore or Boston. Address W. A. Rice, 935 South street, Philadelphia. August 17.

articles.headline: Notice -- desertion (Roxana Matthews / George Matthews)
articles.author: Roxana Matthews
articles.summary: I hereby give notice that George M[atthews] was married to me on June 4th, 18[49?], and has left me some three years ago, and married another woman. Signed Roxana Mat[thews]. (No address given; location not stated.)

articles.headline: Death of Robert Harris -- Union A.M.E. Church resolutions and funeral
articles.summary: Resolutions of the quarterly meeting conference of the Union A.M.E. church (Philadelphia) on the death of Brother Robert Harris, who departed this life after a protracted illness in July 1867 in the city of Philadelphia. He had been a member of the church about twenty-seven years, a class leader and trustee. His Masonic brethren of Eastern Star Lodge, No. 19 (printed), and the members of the church proceeded from his late residence to the church, where Rev. Wm. Moore, elder in charge, delivered a discourse; the funeral cortege proceeded to Olive Cemetery. Committee: Edward Young, Albert H. Hall, Jas. E. Turner; Wm. Moore, Elder in Charge.
people: deceased; member ~27 years, class leader and trustee, Union A.M.E. church; Mason, Eastern Star Lodge No. 19
elder in charge, Union A.M.E. church; delivered funeral discourse (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notes by the Way, No. I (Trip to Wilmington, N.C.)
articles.author: J. M. Brown
articles.summary: Travel letter: left Baltimore Friday July 26th on the Bay Line steamer Geo. Leary to Norfolk, then to Wilmington, N.C. (Rev. Samuel B. Williams, pastor), then Halifax N.C. and Richmond. Reports at length on Mrs. Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, who addressed the colored Baptist and Methodist Sabbath-schools at Wilmington and lectured to some 2000 persons; at Richmond she addressed the people in the House of Delegates of Virginia ('Mrs. Harper in the capital of Virginia'). Visited an orphan asylum near Wilmington (American Missionary Association; matron Mrs. Emily L. Pipper). Signed J. M. Brown, Felton Station, Del., Aug. 12, 1867.
people: lecturer on a southern tour (Philadelphian); addressed Sabbath-schools at Wilmington N.C. and the people in the Virginia House of Delegates at Richmond

articles.headline: Obituary of John O. Moore, Jr.
articles.summary: Eulogistic obituary of John O. Moore, Jr. ('Johnny'), a young man suddenly taken from his parents and friends. No church, address, date or place of death is stated in the notice.

articles.headline: Notice -- piano instruction by a lady (630 Pine St.)
articles.summary: Instruction given on the Piano by a lady; beginners preferred. Address 630 Pine St. (Dated Aug. 24; standing notice, no name given.)

events.name: Lecture by Fanny Jackson at Cape Island (Cape May, N.J.)
events.description: Miss Fanny Jackson, Principal of the Female Department of the Institute for Colored Youth, lectured Tuesday evening, July 23d, 1867, about three-quarters of an hour on education and self-improvement; introduced by Sam'l Whipper, Esq. She was stopping at the residence of Rev. Stephen Smith.
attendees: lecturer; Principal, Female Dept., Institute for Colored Youth (Miss)

events.name: Monthly Communion, Macedonia A.M.E. Church, South Camden, N.J.
events.location: Macedonia A.M.E. Church, South Camden, N.J.
events.description: The monthly communion of Macedonia A.M.E. Church, South Camden, N.J., Sabbath afternoon at 3 o'clock, August 11th; members of sister churches invited. J. B. Hamilton, Pastor.

events.name: Camp Meeting at Evesham, N.J. (Jacob Mitchell, P.I.C.)
events.description: Camp meeting to commence August 15th at Evesham, N.J.; stages from Market St. wharf (fare 75 cents). Rev. Bishop Wayman to be present, with Rev. W. Moore of Philadelphia, Rev. W. W. Grimes of New Jersey, Rev. W. H. Chase of Delaware, and Rev. Woodlin of Brooklyn. Jacob Mitchell, Preacher in charge.

events.name: Camp Meeting at Allentown, N.J. (Peter Gardiner, P.I.C.)
events.description: A camp meeting at Allentown, N.J., commencing August 8th. Committee: Francis Raney, David Brown, Jerr. Johnson, ---- Jones, and others. Peter Gardiner, Preacher-in-Charge.

events.name: Grand Union Excursion of the Camden A.M.E. Sabbath-schools
events.location: South Street Wharf, Philadelphia / Kaighn's Point / Miss Gibson's Woods
events.description: Grand excursion of the Sabbath-schools of A.M.E. Macedonia Church (Camden N.J.), A.M.E. Mission (Kaighnsville N.J.), A.M.E. Mission (Centreville N.J.), and the Deep Cut School, to Miss Gibson's Woods, on the steamer Eagle, Tuesday morning, August 13, 1867; steamer leaves South Street Wharf, Philadelphia, and Kaighn's Point. Tickets 40 cents, children half price.

events.name: Pic-nic -- Union Sabbath-school of Bethel A.M.E. Church of Frankford, to Large's Grove
events.description: The Union Sabbath-school of the A.M.E. Bethel Church of Frankford intend going to Large's Grove on Wednesday, August 21, 1867 (or the 28th if stormy); invitation extended to the Bethel, Union and Wesley Sabbath-schools to participate. Rev. Daniel P. Seaton and other eminent speakers to address the school.

events.name: Union Camp-Meeting at Media (Pa.)
events.location: Media, Pa. (camp ground); trains from depot 31st and Market Sts., Philadelphia
events.description: Time-table published for those desiring to attend the 'Union Camp-meeting' at Media on Sabbath, Sept. 1st. Sunday trains leave the depot at 31st and Market Sts. at 7.45 A.M., 9.30 A.M. and 2 P.M.; a night-train leaves the camp for Philadelphia at 10 P.M.; excursion tickets 75 cents; passenger cars leave Eighth and Market Sts. for the depot half an hour before each train. (OCR shows a 'Dr. Mears, Sec.' line; not confirmed on the image.)

events.name: Grand Sabbath-school Pic-nic and Temperance Meeting, Burlington, N.J. (Jacob Mitchell, pastor)
events.description: A grand Sabbath-school pic-nic at Burlington, N.J., Sept. 12, 1867, in the grove; a Temperance Meeting also to be held the same evening in the church; refreshments on hand. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor.

events.name: Chester County (Pa.) Quarterly Conference and quarterly meetings (Andrew Till, Elder in charge)
events.location: Chester County, Pa. (Coatesville, Centreville, Downingtown, Deep Valley, Phoenixville)
events.description: Quarterly Conference to be held at [Coates?]ville, Chester county, Pa., Sept. 14th, 1867; quarterly meetings at Centreville, Sept. 15th; Downingtown, Sept. 21st and 22d; Deep Valley, Sept. 28th and 29th; Phoenixville, Oct. 5th and 6th, 1867. Andrew Till, Elder in charge.

events.name: Harvest Home -- Green's Tabernacle, No. 6, I.O. of B. & S. of Love and Charity, Woodbury, N.J.
events.description: Green's Tabernacle, No. 6, I.O. of B. & S. (Brothers and Sisters) of Love and Charity, to hold a Harvest Home at Woodbury, N.J., Sept. 19, 1867. Cars leave upper Ferry, Market Street, at 8 and 9 A.M. and 3, 3.30 and 4 P.M. (fare 50 cents); stage from Gloucester at 8 and 10 A.M. and 1 and 4 P.M. (fare 25 cents).
